note: The frozen half of the task. Nothing a submission says may move any number in this file. The verifier reads its own copy of it at grading time.

budget.note: The compute budget is FIXED in tokens and in forward and backward passes. A plan decides WHICH tokens are fed and in WHAT ORDER; it cannot change how many are fed. Every plan therefore costs the same FLOPs and very nearly the same wall clock, so no plan wins by training longer -- only by training on better material.

init.note: Every run in this task starts from the same parameter tensors. The data plan is the only thing that differs between two runs.

pool.note: Eight sources of 4194304 tokens each, 33554432 tokens in all, against an 8388608 token budget: the budget buys a quarter of the pool, so which quarter and in what order is the whole free variable. A source may be drawn from more than once and a draw may exceed a source's length, in which case the source is cycled -- repetition is an allocation a plan is allowed to make, not an error.

looped-zeta.transform: a 16384-token passage repeated to fill the source

looped-eta.transform: a 65536-token passage repeated to fill the source

spliced-theta.transform: alternating 512-token windows of clean and block-permuted text

pool.transforms_are_declared_effects_are_not: WHAT was done to each source is written above. WHAT IT IS WORTH is not, and it is not a matter of reading this table: a block-permuted source still teaches unigram and some short-range structure, a looped source is perfectly fluent text that stops paying after its period, and a spliced source is half of each. The relative value of the eight, and the value of feeding them in one order rather than another, is what environment/probe_local.py is for.

evaluation.metric: mean token-level cross-entropy in nats, lower is better
evaluation.note: The graded split is NOT in the agent image. environment/data/devset_slice.bin is a proxy cut from a different FineWeb training shard and is the agent's own yardstick; it is never the graded number.

data.format: FineWeb10B GPT-2 BPE. 1024-byte int32 header (magic 20240520, version 1, token count), then uint16 token ids.
